articles.title: What Heavenly Modulation Actually Is
articles.dek: A broadcast band that no regulator allocated, because a ministry allocated it instead.
articles.author: jubilee
articles.stands: A frequency is a promise that the same thing is in the same place every time you tune there.

articles.title: Why It Had to Be Music
articles.dek: Scripture teaches itself in songs, and a song is the only sermon anyone repeats on purpose.
articles.author: melody
articles.stands: Moses was told to teach Israel a song, not a lecture — because a song is what they would still have when everything else had been forgotten.

articles.title: Free, and Built to Stay Free
articles.dek: No subscription, no advertising, no pledge drive — and a structural reason it can stay that way.
articles.author: jubilee
articles.stands: Free is not a launch promotion here. It is what is left once you remove the two costs that normally force a price.

articles.title: AI, Pointed at the Kingdom
articles.dek: The music, the voices and the artwork on this band are AI-made. Here is why that is said out loud.
articles.author: amir
articles.stands: A tool is judged by what it is pointed at. The same technology filling the world with noise can be turned to carry the Word into it.

articles.title: Can a Machine Worship?
articles.dek: No. And the answer matters more than the question, because of what it tells you this band is for.
articles.author: nova
articles.stands: The organ does not worship either. Nobody has ever thought that was an argument against organs.

articles.title: What We Will Never Let AI Decide
articles.dek: A short list, published on purpose, so that it can be held against us.
articles.author: zev
articles.stands: A boundary nobody wrote down is not a boundary. It is an intention, and intentions drift quietly under deadline.

articles.title: Who Wrote This Song?
articles.dek: The whole credit chain for one track, from the passage it stands on to the play log.
articles.author: caleb
articles.stands: Every step that required a decision was made by a person. Every step that required labour was not.

articles.title: The Cost of a Station, Then and Now
articles.dek: Why round-the-clock gospel radio in a minority language was, until very recently, simply unaffordable.
articles.author: amir
articles.stands: The gospel was never the thing in short supply. The transmitters were.

articles.title: Every Tool the Church Was Afraid Of
articles.dek: The press, radio, television, the internet — the same argument each time, and what being late cost.
articles.author: elias
articles.stands: The fears were right about the risk and wrong about the conclusion, every single time.

articles.title: Everywhere There Is a Signal
articles.dek: Served from the edge, built for cheap phones and thin connections, with no app to install.
articles.author: zariah
articles.stands: Free at the point of listening is a small detail where everyone has a card on file, and an enormous one everywhere else.

articles.title: Twelve Voices, and None of Them Are Strangers
articles.dek: A playlist has no host, which is why a playlist never becomes a habit.
articles.author: nova
articles.stands: A listener in a hard week is not handed an algorithm. They are handed a voice that sounds like it already knows what kind of week it has been.

articles.title: A Frequency Nobody Has to Pay to Reach
articles.dek: Terrestrial Christian radio runs on an auction. This band removes the auction.
articles.author: elias
articles.stands: A station exists here because someone needed that station to exist — not because of what it could sell against.

articles.title: The First Thing Anyone Did After the Sea Closed
articles.dek: Exodus 15 — deliverance happens, and the immediate response is a song.
articles.author: zev
articles.stands: Not a report. Not a monument. A song, with a woman leading it and a tambourine in her hand.

articles.title: Lament Has a Frequency Too
articles.dek: Why there are stations for grief and for walking out of addiction, and not only for praise.
articles.author: eliana
articles.stands: Roughly a third of the Psalms are complaints. A dial that only knows how to celebrate is missing most of the songbook.

articles.title: The Song You Sang at Eleven and Still Know
articles.dek: Why the children’s stations on this band are not the easy end of it.
articles.author: melody
articles.stands: Whatever is put into a child in song is still going to be in there in fifty years. That is not a small responsibility.

articles.title: Every Worship Song Is Talking to Two People at Once
articles.dek: One line goes up. The next goes sideways. Most songs never announce that they are doing both.
articles.author: jubilee
articles.stands: Sing it to God and it is prayer. Sing it beside somebody and it is teaching. It is always doing both.

articles.title: A Dial That Keeps the Kingdom Calendar
articles.dek: From Friday sundown the whole band changes character, and nobody flips a switch.
articles.author: zev
articles.stands: Secular radio breathes with the retail calendar. This one breathes with Yahuah’s.

articles.title: Every Song Carries the Word with It
articles.dek: A track here is not just audio. It carries the Scripture it stands on.
articles.author: caleb
articles.stands: Passive listening becomes encounter without the listener having to do anything but leave it on.

articles.title: What a SongID Is, and Why You Should Care
articles.dek: Twelve characters that turn a song from a file into a fixed object.
articles.author: caleb
articles.stands: Anything that can be quietly swapped will eventually be quietly swapped, if only by accident.

articles.title: The Schedule Is Published Before It Airs
articles.dek: Two listeners tuning in at the same second hear the same song. That is the whole difference between a band and a shuffle.
articles.author: zev
articles.stands: A shuffle gives everybody their own private radio station. That sounds generous, and it dissolves the one thing radio was for.

articles.title: How a Frequency Gets Assigned
articles.dek: The life of a station, from a need somebody could state in a sentence to the moment it signs on.
articles.author: jubilee
articles.stands: The number is reserved at the beginning, when the station is still only a need with a remit attached.

articles.title: Hosted in the Language, Not Translated into It
articles.dek: Stations written in their own languages rather than run through a translator.
articles.author: santiago
articles.stands: A believer in Bucharest or Lagos or Seoul gets a station that sounds like home, on the same dial as everyone else.

articles.title: Twenty Languages, and the Ones Still Missing
articles.dek: Naming the gaps out loud, because a list of what is missing is more use than a list of what is done.
articles.author: eliana
articles.stands: A gap nobody names is a gap nobody fills.

articles.title: Where This Band Is Going
articles.dek: A map, a set of assigned frequencies, and an honest account of what is not known yet.
articles.author: zariah
articles.stands: The frequencies are the plan, written down where anybody can hold us to them.

articles.title: How to Use a Radio Band You Cannot Buy a Radio For
articles.dek: The dial, the player that never stops, favourites, and how to hand somebody a frequency.
articles.author: melody
articles.stands: Press play once and it keeps playing wherever you go on the site. That is the whole design.

articles.title: Leave It On
articles.dek: The case for a house with something true playing in it that nobody had to choose.
articles.author: eliana
articles.stands: The songs that formed you were mostly not the ones you selected. They were the ones that happened to be on.

articles.title: For the Person Who Stopped Going
articles.dek: No argument, no guilt, and nothing you have to sign up for.
articles.author: nova
articles.stands: You do not have to have worked out what you believe before you are allowed to listen to something.

articles.title: Still Being Built, on Purpose
articles.dek: Frequencies are reserved before their stations are finished, and the dial keeps growing.
articles.author: caleb
articles.stands: The dial you tune next month will not be the dial you tuned today, and that is the plan rather than an apology.

articles.title: What Is Actually Broadcasting Today
articles.dek: The live count, the station names, and the discipline behind what reaches the air.
articles.author: imani
articles.stands: A frequency is reserved before a station is finished, the same way a broadcaster holds a licence.

articles.title: Doubt Is Not the Opposite of Faith. Certainty Is.
articles.dek: The thing almost nobody says to a person who has started asking questions.
articles.author: nova
articles.stands: Faith is what you do while you are not sure. If you were sure, it would not be faith. It would be arithmetic.

articles.title: The Questions You Were Told Not to Ask in Church
articles.dek: Not because they are dangerous, but because somebody in the room did not have an answer.
articles.author: nova
articles.stands: A question that gets shut down does not go away. It goes underground, and it takes the person with it.

articles.title: You Can Come Back Without Explaining Where You Went
articles.dek: The debrief nobody owes anybody, and the station built on not asking for one.
articles.author: nova
articles.stands: The father in that parable runs down the road before the son gets a word out. The speech the son prepared is never actually needed.

articles.title: Why Midnight Praise Exists
articles.dek: Three in the morning has its own theology, and almost nothing is scheduled for it.
articles.author: nova
articles.stands: Paul and Silas sang at midnight. The text records the hour, and Scripture does not usually waste words on the time.

articles.title: Hymns Survive Because They Were Written by People in Trouble
articles.dek: Not heritage, and not nostalgia — the ones that lasted were forged in the worst year of somebody’s life.
articles.author: nova
articles.stands: A hymn is a sentence somebody had to mean under pressure. That is why it holds weight the next person can lean on.

articles.title: What Wisdom Is, When Advice Has Run Out
articles.dek: Advice tells you what to do. Wisdom is for the situations where nobody can.
articles.author: nova
articles.stands: Job’s friends gave superb advice for seven days after they stopped sitting with him in silence. The silence was the wise part.

articles.title: Nothing Here Is Trying to Close the Deal
articles.dek: An editorial policy, stated plainly, so you can hold the station to it.
articles.author: nova
articles.stands: If a thing is true, it does not need a technique. If it needs a technique, that is worth noticing about the thing.

articles.title: What Plays on the Flagship, and Why That Is the Hardest Choice
articles.dek: A station for everybody is the most difficult remit on the dial, not the easiest.
articles.author: jubilee
articles.stands: A specialist station only has to be right for its listener. The flagship has to be right for a stranger.

articles.title: A House Where Four Generations Have to Agree on the Radio
articles.dek: The real design problem behind a family station, and why most of them solve it badly.
articles.author: jubilee
articles.stands: Most family radio is aimed at the parent and endured by everybody else. That is not a family station. It is a parent station with hostages.

articles.title: The Ones You Make Before You Know They Were Decisions
articles.dek: Almost nothing that changes a life arrives labelled as a fork in the road.
articles.author: jubilee
articles.stands: The large decisions announce themselves and get prayed over. The ones that actually set the direction are made in about four seconds.

articles.title: Celebrating Yeshua Without Borrowing the World’s Party
articles.dek: Joy is not the same thing as a loud room, and the difference is audible.
articles.author: jubilee
articles.stands: The world knows how to throw a party and cannot manufacture the reason for one. We have the reason and keep borrowing the party.

articles.title: When Faith Feels Hard Is Not a Beginner Station
articles.dek: The people who need it most have usually been at this for decades.
articles.author: jubilee
articles.stands: Nobody warns you that the hardest stretch tends to arrive in year twenty, to someone doing everything right.

articles.title: Why the Flagship Never Plays a Song Twice in a Day
articles.dek: Commercial radio repeats its best track every four hours. Here is the argument against.
articles.author: jubilee
articles.stands: Repetition is how you build a hit, and familiarity is not the same thing as agreement.

articles.title: Jazz Is What Worship Sounds Like When Nobody Is Performing
articles.dek: A form built on listening to each other rather than on delivering a rehearsed thing.
articles.author: jubilee
articles.stands: The whole form is people listening to each other closely enough to respond in real time. There are worse descriptions of a church.

articles.title: Family Faith Is Mostly Logistics
articles.dek: The unglamorous truth, and why admitting it takes the guilt out of the whole subject.
articles.author: melody
articles.stands: Nobody teaches this because it does not sound spiritual. It is, however, the part that decides whether any of the rest happens.

articles.title: What a Sanctuary Sounds Like When It Is a Kitchen
articles.dek: The word does not mean a building. It means a place where something is protected.
articles.author: melody
articles.stands: A sanctuary is not a quiet room. It is a place where a particular thing is safe, and quiet is optional.

articles.title: The Twenty Minutes in the Car Are the Discipleship
articles.dek: Side by side, no eye contact, and a fixed end point. It is a nearly perfect format.
articles.author: melody
articles.stands: A child will tell you things at forty miles an hour that they would never say across a table.

articles.title: Children Do Not Need a Simplified God
articles.dek: Simple language, yes. A smaller God, no — and children can tell the difference immediately.
articles.author: melody
articles.stands: Simplifying the words is respect. Simplifying the subject is a debt, and it comes due in the teenage years with interest.

articles.title: Beyond the Trauma Is Not the Same as over It
articles.dek: A station name that is doing careful work, and a distinction most recovery language misses.
articles.author: melody
articles.stands: Beyond means you have travelled. It does not mean the ground behind you has changed.

articles.title: What Actually Grows Back, and What Does Not
articles.dek: Restoration is a real promise and a specific one. It is not the same as replacement.
articles.author: melody
articles.stands: Joel promises the years the locusts ate will be restored. It does not promise the locusts never came.

articles.title: Whose Job Is It to Teach Your Children the Words?
articles.dek: The uncomfortable one, asked plainly, with no guilt attached to the answer.
articles.author: melody
articles.stands: An hour a week against everything else a child hears is not a fair contest, and it was never designed to be one.

articles.title: Riddim Was Church Before It Was Radio
articles.dek: The rhythm arrived in the sanctuary first. The charts came along later and took the credit.
articles.author: zariah
articles.stands: The drum was not borrowed from the dancehall. Both of them got it from the same place, and the church got there first.

articles.title: Worshipping in a Country That Is Not Yours
articles.dek: The particular loneliness of praising God in a place where your praise is an accent.
articles.author: zariah
articles.stands: You can be entirely welcome in a church and still be the only person in it who knows what the song is supposed to feel like.

articles.title: Why the French Station Is Not a Translation of the English One
articles.dek: It has a different playlist, a different pace and a different set of concerns, on purpose.
articles.author: zariah
articles.stands: A dubbed station is a station about somebody else, delivered in your language. That is not the same as a station for you.

articles.title: The Commute Is the Only Hour That Belongs to You
articles.dek: Nobody can reach you, nothing is expected, and it is the last unclaimed slot in most days.
articles.author: zariah
articles.stands: Everybody wants that hour. Most days it is the only one where you get to decide what goes in.

articles.title: Holidays Are Where the Old Country Survives
articles.dek: Language goes first, then food, then the songs. The feast days are where the last of it holds on.
articles.author: zariah
articles.stands: A grandchild who cannot hold a conversation in the language will still know every word of the song that gets sung once a year.

articles.title: A Rhythm Your Grandmother Would Recognise
articles.dek: Continuity is not conservatism. It is the test of whether a thing was ever really yours.
articles.author: zariah
articles.stands: If your grandmother could not find her way into it, something got replaced rather than developed.

articles.title: Praying in the Language You Dream In
articles.dek: Fluency is not the issue. There is a language a person is most themselves in, and God speaks it.
articles.author: zariah
articles.stands: You can be perfectly fluent in a language and still not be able to be honest in it.

articles.title: Courage Is Mostly Boring
articles.dek: The word gets used for the dramatic version. Almost all of the real thing is repetitive and unwitnessed.
articles.author: caleb
articles.stands: Nobody is ever going to congratulate you for the thing that actually took courage, because nobody is going to know it happened.

articles.title: Iron Sharpening Iron Requires Two Pieces of Iron
articles.dek: The verse gets quoted at men who have no such friendship, as if naming it produced one.
articles.author: caleb
articles.stands: Sharpening makes a noise, removes material, and cannot be done at a distance. Most of what men call friendship is none of those.

articles.title: Marriage Matters Is Not a Conference
articles.dek: A weekend produces resolve. A marriage runs on Tuesdays, and nothing is scheduled for Tuesdays.
articles.author: caleb
articles.stands: The intensive weekend has an excellent record on how people feel by Sunday night and almost none on where they are in March.

articles.title: After the Storm: The Part Nobody Films
articles.dek: The testimony ends at the rescue. The clearing up takes years and has no audience.
articles.author: caleb
articles.stands: Every testimony you have heard was edited to end at the good bit, and everybody listening quietly concluded that theirs was going wrong.

articles.title: Acapella Is What Is Left When the Production Stops
articles.dek: Strip the arrangement and you find out whether the song was ever carrying anything.
articles.author: caleb
articles.stands: Production can make a weak line feel enormous. Take it away and the line has to be enormous by itself, or it is just a sentence.

articles.title: The Last Ten Minutes of the Day Belong to Somebody
articles.dek: Whatever occupies them is what the mind works on all night. That slot is worth defending.
articles.author: caleb
articles.stands: You do not get to choose what you think about at four in the morning. You do get to choose what you handed yourself at eleven.

articles.title: Why a Young Man Needs a Station and Not a Podcast
articles.dek: One of these builds a habit. The other builds an appetite, and they are not the same.
articles.author: caleb
articles.stands: A podcast asks you to choose it every time. Anything that has to be chosen every time eventually will not be.

articles.title: The Feasts Are Not Jewish Nostalgia. They Are a Calendar.
articles.dek: Everyone keeps a calendar. The only question is whose, and what it is quietly teaching.
articles.author: zev
articles.stands: A calendar is a curriculum. It decides what you think about, in what order, every year, whether or not you agreed to it.

articles.title: What Happens When the Law Is Set to Music
articles.dek: It stops being a list of rules and starts being something you can carry around.
articles.author: zev
articles.stands: The instruction to memorise it comes with an instruction about how. Write it as a song, and put it in their mouths.

articles.title: Shema Means Hear, and Then It Means Do
articles.dek: A word with no clean English equivalent, and a whole posture lost in the translation.
articles.author: zev
articles.stands: In English you can hear a thing perfectly and do nothing about it, and no one has misused the word. In Hebrew that is not available.

articles.title: The Subject Every Station Avoids at the Same Time
articles.dek: Scripture discusses money constantly. Christian radio discusses it almost never, and the reason is not mysterious.
articles.author: zev
articles.stands: A station funded by its listeners cannot teach freely about money. It has a position, and everyone can hear it.

articles.title: Washing Feet Before Anyone Is Watching
articles.dek: The gesture has been thoroughly domesticated. What it originally demonstrated was rank.
articles.author: zev
articles.stands: It was the job given to whoever in the household had the least standing. That is the whole content of the demonstration.

articles.title: Identity in Yeshua Is Not a Personality Type
articles.dek: The word has been absorbed by an industry that means something else by it entirely.
articles.author: zev
articles.stands: One of these is discovered by looking inward and describing what is there. The other is conferred, from outside, by somebody else.

articles.title: Why Heaven’s Dawn Airs Before Sunrise
articles.dek: The day starts the night before on this calendar, and the schedule follows it.
articles.author: zev
articles.stands: And there was evening, and there was morning — the first day. The order in that sentence is not decorative.

articles.title: Fire Is Not Volume
articles.dek: The correction Pentecostal radio needs most, from inside the tradition rather than outside it.
articles.author: imani
articles.stands: Elijah gets wind, earthquake and fire, and the text says God was in none of them. Then a low voice, and he covers his face.

articles.title: Ten Days of Waiting Before One Day of Fire
articles.dek: Everybody preaches the second chapter. The first one is where the people actually live.
articles.author: imani
articles.stands: They were told to wait, with no date given, in a city that had recently executed their teacher. The waiting is not the preamble. It is most of the account.

articles.title: Africa Is Not a Mission Field on This Dial. It Is a Broadcaster.
articles.dek: The direction of travel assumed by most Christian media is a century out of date.
articles.author: imani
articles.stands: The centre of gravity of the Church moved decades ago. Most of the media has not been told.

articles.title: What Yorùbá Praise Does That a Translation Cannot
articles.dek: In a tonal language the melody is not decoration on the words. It is part of them.
articles.author: imani
articles.stands: Change the pitch and you have not changed the tune. You have changed the word.

articles.title: Amharic Worship Sounds Ancient Because It Is
articles.dek: Ethiopia was Christian before most of Europe, and the music never went through the West.
articles.author: imani
articles.stands: This is not an old-sounding style. It is an old style, developed continuously, that simply never passed through anybody else’s hands.

articles.title: Praying in Swahili at Three in the Morning
articles.dek: A continuous prayer frequency, and why the hour it is hardest to pray is the hour it is left running.
articles.author: imani
articles.stands: Somewhere it is always three in the morning, and somebody is always awake with something they cannot put down.

articles.title: Inspire Chill Is Still a Pentecostal Station
articles.dek: Quiet is not the absence of the Spirit. Sometimes it is the more honest report of it.
articles.author: imani
articles.stands: A tradition that can only recognise God at high intensity has accidentally taught its people that most of their life is godless.

articles.title: La Familia Is a Doctrine, Not a Demographic
articles.dek: Marketing treats it as an audience segment. It is closer to an ecclesiology.
articles.author: santiago
articles.stands: The household is the unit Scripture keeps addressing. Everywhere else has spent a century breaking it into individuals and selling to each.

articles.title: Why There Is a Latin Station Sung in English
articles.dek: It looks like a mistake on the schedule. It is the station for people who live between two languages.
articles.author: santiago
articles.stands: The second generation does not need a Spanish station or an English one. It needs the one that knows both are true at once.

articles.title: Portuguese Is Not Spanish, and Brasil Gets Its Own Frequency
articles.dek: A distinction constantly flattened by people who have never had to listen closely.
articles.author: santiago
articles.stands: Two hundred million people, an entirely separate musical tradition, and a language routinely treated as a regional accent.

articles.title: Two Generations, One Kitchen, Different Languages
articles.dek: The everyday negotiation of an immigrant household, and what a radio station can do about it.
articles.author: santiago
articles.stands: The parents are most themselves in one language and the children in another, and nobody chose this.

articles.title: Praying Out Loud Is a Cultural Habit Worth Keeping
articles.dek: Some traditions pray audibly in front of each other as a matter of course. That is not a small inheritance.
articles.author: santiago
articles.stands: A child who has heard adults pray out loud, badly, at the kitchen table, has been given something no curriculum supplies.

articles.title: Focus Is a Spiritual Discipline with a Soundtrack
articles.dek: Attention is the raw material of prayer, work and love, and it is the thing most under attack.
articles.author: santiago
articles.stands: You cannot pray, work or love anybody with an attention span that has been trained to turn over every nine seconds.

articles.title: Wellness Without the Religion of Wellness
articles.dek: Rest, food, sleep and the body are genuinely spiritual subjects. The industry around them is a competing faith.
articles.author: santiago
articles.stands: One of these says look after the body because it is not yours. The other says perfect the body because it is all there is.

articles.title: The Gospel Arrived Here in the Wrong Hands. It Is Still the Gospel.
articles.dek: Both halves of that sentence are true, and most people are only willing to say one of them.
articles.author: tahoma
articles.stands: The message was carried by people who also carried a great deal else. Sorting one from the other is the work of several generations, and it is not optional.

articles.title: Sobriety Is a Daily Frequency, Not a Testimony
articles.dek: The story gets told once. The thing itself has to be done again tomorrow, and the day after.
articles.author: tahoma
articles.stands: A testimony has an ending. Recovery does not, and the mismatch between those two shapes does real damage.

articles.title: For Men with Nowhere to Be Honest
articles.dek: Not a shortage of friends. A shortage of rooms in which the true answer is sayable.
articles.author: tahoma
articles.stands: Most men have people to talk to and nowhere to say the actual sentence. Those are different shortages and only one of them gets discussed.

articles.title: Anxious No More Is a Command, Which Is the Problem with It
articles.dek: Taking apart the name of one of our own stations, because the misreading is doing harm.
articles.author: tahoma
articles.stands: Be anxious for nothing is not an instruction to feel differently. It is an instruction about where to put the thing.

articles.title: Be Still Is the Hardest Instruction in Scripture
articles.dek: Harder than the ethical commands, because there is nothing to do in order to comply.
articles.author: tahoma
articles.stands: Every other command can be obeyed by doing something. This one is disobeyed by doing anything.

articles.title: The Rhythm That Outlasted the Hymnbook
articles.dek: What happened to island and Native worship after the missionaries stopped supervising it.
articles.author: tahoma
articles.stands: The hymn was imposed, learned, kept, and then quietly rebuilt into something the people who imposed it would not recognise.

articles.title: Stories Are How a People Keep What Cannot Be Written Down
articles.dek: Oral tradition is not a primitive stage before literacy. It is a different technology with different strengths.
articles.author: tahoma
articles.stands: A written text survives without anybody caring about it. A spoken one only survives inside a community that is still telling it, which is a stricter test.

articles.title: The Church That Was Already There When the Missionaries Arrived
articles.dek: Christianity reached India and Central Asia long before it reached most of Europe.
articles.author: amir
articles.stands: The nineteenth-century missionaries who arrived in Kerala met congregations whose liturgy was older than their own countries’ conversion.

articles.title: The Ancient Paths Were Walked by People Who Looked Like Me
articles.dek: Ask for the old paths, says Jeremiah. It is worth checking whose old paths we mean.
articles.author: amir
articles.stands: Everything in the book happened in Asia, to Asians, in Asian languages, in a climate most Western church art has never depicted.

articles.title: Arabic Was a Language of Worship Long Before It Was Anything Else
articles.dek: There were Arabic-speaking Christians before there was anything else for the language to be famous for.
articles.author: amir
articles.stands: Arab Christians were praying in Arabic centuries before the seventh century, and have never stopped.

articles.title: The Bengali Station Exists Because the Gap Was Indefensible
articles.dek: One of the most spoken languages on earth, and almost nothing on the air in it.
articles.author: amir
articles.stands: Nobody decided Bengali did not matter. It simply never cleared a commercial threshold, which produced the same result.

articles.title: Hindi Worship Is Not Western Worship with Different Words
articles.dek: A different scale system, a different relationship to repetition, and a different idea of what a song is for.
articles.author: amir
articles.stands: Set a Hindi text over a Western chord progression and you have not localised anything. You have made a translation with a costume on.

articles.title: Praying in a Language Your Government Would Rather You Didn’t
articles.dek: For listeners where this is not a hobby, and where the volume knob is a real decision.
articles.author: amir
articles.stands: A great deal of the New Testament was written to people for whom this was the ordinary condition, and it shows in what the text bothers to say.

articles.title: What the Five-Fold Actually Is, and Why It Is Not a Hierarchy
articles.dek: A list of functions has been read for a century as an org chart, with predictable results.
articles.author: amir
articles.stands: The passage names five things the church needs done. It does not name five ranks, and it does not put anybody above anybody.

articles.title: Repentance Is Not an Emotion. It Is a Turn.
articles.dek: The word means to change direction. Feeling bad is optional and frequently a substitute.
articles.author: elias
articles.stands: You can feel terrible for thirty years and never once turn around. Many people have, and they think it counts.

articles.title: Country Music Never Stopped Being Honest About Sin
articles.dek: It kept a vocabulary that most Christian music dropped, and it kept it in the first person.
articles.author: elias
articles.stands: One of these traditions will sing about a man who has ruined his life and is not sure he will stop. The other one moved on from that some time ago.

articles.title: The Two Shortest Prayers in Scripture
articles.dek: Yes and amen. Both are agreements, and both are harder to mean than they look.
articles.author: elias
articles.stands: Amen is not a full stop. It is a signature, and it commits the person who says it.

articles.title: Raising Arrows Is a Long Job with No Applause
articles.dek: The metaphor is about release, and about a result you will not be present to see.
articles.author: elias
articles.stands: An arrow is not for keeping. The entire purpose of the work is that the thing leaves your hand.

articles.title: What Is Given Daily Cannot Be Stockpiled
articles.dek: The manna rotted overnight on purpose, and everybody has tried to store it anyway.
articles.author: elias
articles.stands: They were given exactly one day’s worth, and what they hoarded bred worms. The lesson was not about food.

articles.title: The Churches That Sang Under Surveillance
articles.dek: Romanian praise carries a memory of what it cost, and the music is different because of it.
articles.author: elias
articles.stands: A congregation that knew an informer was in the room learned to mean every word, because those were the words being reported.

articles.title: Purpose Found Is Usually Purpose Assigned
articles.dek: The search is conducted inward. Almost every case in the text runs the other way.
articles.author: elias
articles.stands: Almost nobody in Scripture discovers their purpose. It is handed to them, usually while they are busy with something else, and usually unwelcome.

articles.title: Strong and Sober Are Two Different Achievements
articles.dek: Stopping is one job. Becoming someone who does not need to start is another, and it takes much longer.
articles.author: eliana
articles.stands: Sobriety is a state you can hold by force. Strength is what means you no longer have to.

articles.title: Grief Walked, Not Grief Solved
articles.dek: The station name is the thesis. Nothing here is going to fix it, and that is the offer.
articles.author: eliana
articles.stands: Almost everything said to a grieving person is an attempt to make the sentence stop. Walking alongside is the one response that does not.

articles.title: Stillwater Is Not Background Music
articles.dek: Quiet music that is doing something is not the same as quiet music that is filling a gap.
articles.author: eliana
articles.stands: Ambient music is designed not to be noticed. This is designed to be sat with, which is a different brief entirely.

articles.title: Friendship Is the Least Discussed Means of Grace
articles.dek: Prayer, Scripture, sacrament, and then a category the Church talks about almost never.
articles.author: eliana
articles.stands: Ask what sustained somebody through the worst decade of their life and you will very rarely be told about a discipline.

articles.title: Japan’s Church Is Tiny and Its Martyrs Are Four Hundred Years Old
articles.dek: One of the smallest Christian populations in the developed world, and one of the most extraordinary histories.
articles.author: eliana
articles.stands: For roughly two centuries there were no priests, no Bibles and no buildings, and when the doors finally opened the faith was still there.

articles.title: Tagalog Worship Travels with the People Who Leave
articles.dek: A diaspora scattered across every time zone, mostly working, mostly alone on the significant days.
articles.author: eliana
articles.stands: Filipino workers are in nearly every country on earth, and a great many of them spend Christmas on somebody else’s schedule.

articles.title: What a Station Sounds Like Before Anyone Is Listening
articles.dek: Every frequency on this band spent time playing to nobody, and how it behaved then is the whole test.
articles.author: eliana
articles.stands: The audience arrives, if it arrives, long after the standard has been set. Nothing improves once people are watching.
